BURSEVI:v10p318/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r1.claim: The afterlife is better in its pure, lasting pleasure; worldly pleasure is temporary and mixed with harm, so preferring it merits rebuke.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r1.anchor: حال من فاعل تؤثرون مؤكدة للتوبيخ والعتاب

BURSEVI:v10p318/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r2.claim: The outer appearance of things is like a shell and inner realities like a kernel: the kernel lasts, while the discarded shell quickly perishes.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r2.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن ظواهر الأشياء بالنسبة إلى حقائقها كالقشر بالنسبة إلى اللب

BURSEVI:v10p318/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r3.claim: People devoted to outward appearances prefer fleeting, inferior things because they are veiled from the Hereafter; people of inner truth choose the lasting life with God.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r3.anchor: القشر يؤثرون الأمور الظاهر الخسيسة الدنية الفنية على الأمور الباطنة المعنوية

BURSEVI:v10p318/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r5.claim: The afterlife's reward and purification of the soul, completion of knowledge and obedience, and warning against worldly distraction are truths shared by earlier scriptures.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ذكر من قوله تعالى : {قد أفلح من تزكى

QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.claim: People prefer sensory life and its ornaments, thereby neglecting remembrance of the divine name and prayer because they lack purification; the true spiritual life is better and more enduring.
QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.anchor: تغفلون وتحتجبون عن ذكر ذلك الاسم وصلاة الرب بالحياة الحسية وطيباتها وزخارفها لعدم التزكية

SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.speaker: أبو العباس الدينوري
SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.claim: Low character and ambition choose the world's lowliness; elevated ambition chooses the afterlife, while noble states and sound realities prefer their Lord over both worlds and all they contain.
SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو العباس الدينوري : من خسأ طبعه وحقرت همته آثر الدنيا بخستها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r1.claim: The statement that the afterlife is better and more lasting reinforces the rebuke: they have turned from considering what is superior and enduring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r1.anchor: وجملة : { والآخرة خير وأبقى } عطف على جملة التوبيخ عطف الخبر على الإنشاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r2.claim: Abqā is a comparative meaning longer in duration; a Prophetic garment report uses it similarly for what is more pious and lasting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r2.anchor: و { أبقى } : اسم تفضيل ، أي أطول بقاء ، وفي حديث النهي عن جر الإزار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r13.speaker: عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r13.claim: Umar compares everything worldly relative to the afterlife to a rabbit's sneeze, stressing its insignificance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r13.anchor: وقال عمر: ما في الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كنفخة أرنب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#2/r1.claim: The afterlife—the Garden—is better for the Prophet and more lasting than this world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#2/r1.anchor: والآخرة خير لك يعني الجنة أفضل وأبقى أي أدوم من الدنيا

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r2.claim: The Hereafter is better and more lasting because worldly pleasure is slight, interrupted, and mixed with annoyances, while the next life’s pleasure endures unspoiled.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r2.anchor: لأن نعيم الدنيا قليل وينقطع، ومشوب بكل منغص

KASHSHAF:87:17/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:17/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:17/r1.claim: The afterlife is better in its own qualities, more delightful, and more lasting.

KASHSHAF:87:17/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:17/r2.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF:87:17/r2.claim: ʿUmar compares worldly life within the afterlife to the brief sneeze of a rabbit.
KASHSHAF:87:17/r2.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه : ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كنفجة أرنب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r17.claim: One reading says the afterlife is better for believers than worldly life and its recompense lasts longer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r17.anchor: خير للمؤمن من الدنيا , وأبقى للجزاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r18.claim: He reads the comparison as better in goodness and more lasting in permanence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r19.claim: A further possibility is that the afterlife is better for the obedient and more lasting for the people of Paradise.

MUQATIL:87:14-19/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r3.claim: The Hereafter is better and more enduring than worldly life.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#6/r1.claim: The hereafter is better in its own right and more enduring.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r1.claim: The afterlife means Paradise; it is better and more enduring than this world.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r1.anchor: أي والدار الآخرة أي الجنة. { خير } أي أفضل. { وأبقى } أي أدوم من الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r2.claim: A hadith likens this world against the afterlife to the water a finger brings back from the sea; Qurtubi marks it authentic.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r2.anchor: ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كما يضع أحدكم أصبعه في اليم، فلينظر بم يرجع

QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r3.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r3.claim: Even if this world were perishable gold and the afterlife lasting pottery, one should choose the latter; in reality their relative worth is the reverse.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:17/r3.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: لو كانت الدنيا من ذهب يفنى، والآخرة من خزف يبقى، لكان الواجب

NAHHAS:v5p207/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r13.claim: The phrase al-ākhiratu khayrun wa-abqā is a nominal sentence with subject and predicate.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:17/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:17/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:17/r1.claim: The afterlife is superior in kind and longer in duration; preferring worldly life over it is foolish misjudgment no clear-sighted person would make.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:17/r1.anchor: خير في نوعها ، وأبقى في أمدها

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r1.claim: Whatever is better and more enduring is more deserving of preference, so the afterlife ought to be preferred over the worldly life people choose.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r1.anchor: كل ما كان خيرا وأبقى فهو آثر ، فيلزم أن تكون الآخرة آثر من الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r2.claim: The afterlife surpasses this world because it combines bodily and spiritual happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r2.anchor: الآخرة مشتملة على السعادة الجسمانية والروحانية ، والدنيا ليست كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r3.claim: Worldly pleasures are mixed with pains, whereas afterlife pleasures are not.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r3.anchor: أن الدنيا لذاتها مخلوطة بالآلام ، والآخرة ليست كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r4.claim: The afterlife lasts while worldly life passes away; permanence is better than transience.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#2/r4.anchor: أن الدنيا فانية ، والآخرة باقية ، والباقي خير من الفاني

SAMIN-DURR:87:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:17/r1.claim: The thing surpassed in endurance by the Hereafter is worldly life.

STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.claim: A hadith compares the world to a prison for the believer and a garden for the disbeliever.
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.anchor: a ḥadīth states, “The world is the prison of the believer and the garden of the disbeliever”

TAB:87:17/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:17/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:17/r1.claim: People prefer the adornment of worldly life, but the afterlife is better in goodness and more enduring because this life ends while the next does not.
TAB:87:17/r1.anchor: وقوله :  بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدّنيْا يقول للناس :  بل تؤثرون أيها الناس زينة الحياة الدنيا

TAB:87:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:17/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:17/r2.claim: Qatāda says people choose the immediate life except those God protects; the next life is better in goodness and permanence.
TAB:87:17/r2.anchor: عن قتادة بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدّنيْا فاختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله

TAB:87:17/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:17/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB:87:17/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd stops at this verse and confesses that people prefer worldly luxuries because those are visible while the afterlife is hidden.
TAB:87:17/r3.anchor: عن عَرْفَجَة الثقفيّ ،   قال :  استقرأت ابن مسعود سَبّحِ اسْمَ رَبّكَ الأعْلَى ،   فلما بلغ

TAB:87:17/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:17/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
TAB:87:17/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person, understanding it to refer to the wretched people.
TAB:87:17/r4.anchor: إلا أبا عمرو ،   فإنه قرأه بالياء ،   وقال :  يعني الأشقياء .

TAB:87:17/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:17/r5.speaker: author
TAB:87:17/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the second-person reading, followed by the consensus of readers; Ubayy's reading with antum also supports it.
TAB:87:17/r5.anchor: والذي لا أوثر عليه في قراءة ذلك التاء ،   لإجماع الحجة من القرّاء عليه .

TAB:87:17/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:17/r6.speaker: أبي
TAB:87:17/r6.claim: Ubayy's recitation adds antum before the second-person verb, further supporting that reading.
TAB:87:17/r6.anchor: وذُكر أن ذلك في قراءة أُبيّ :  بَلْ أنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ فذلك أيضا شاهد لصحة القراءة بالتاء .

TAB:87:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the demonstrative covers the nearby verses about purification, prayer, preferring this life, and the better, lasting afterlife, since this is the nearest referent; ṣuḥuf means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ،   قول من قال :  إن قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكى وَذَكَرَ اسمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that “this” refers to the nearest preceding lines, 87:14–17, because a demonstrative most naturally points to what is nearby; ṣuḥuf means books or scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.anchor: وإنما قلت: ذلك أولى بالصحة من غيره، لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر، فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r1.claim: The afterlife is better and more enduring than worldly life; the comparison needs only its relative superiority, although the afterlife is eternal in itself.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r1.anchor: عد الآخرة أبقى بالنسبة إلى الدنيا مع أنها باقية أبدية في نفسها لأن المقام مقام الترجيح بين الدنيا والآخرة

TABRISI:87:10-17/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r20.claim: The Hereafter, meaning Paradise, is better and more enduring than the worldly life.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r20.anchor: أي والدار الآخرة وهي الجنة { خير } أي أفضل { وأبقى } وأدوم من الدنيا

TABRISI:87:18-19/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:18-19/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:18-19/r7.claim: A transmitted saying warns that loving the Hereafter costs worldly advantage, while loving the world costs advantage in the Hereafter.
TABRISI:87:18-19/r7.anchor: من أحب آخرته أضر بدنياه ومن أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

THALABI:v10p185/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p185/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī takes ‘this’ in the earlier scriptures statement to refer from ‘successful is one who purifies’ through the end of the sura; Ibn Zayd refers it to ‘the afterlife is better and more lasting.’
THALABI:v10p185/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني من قوله: قد أفلح من تزكى إلى آخر السورة، وقال ابن زيد يعني قوله: والآخرة خير وأبقى

THALABI:v10p185/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p185/r7.claim: Qatāda says God's books repeatedly state that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
THALABI:v10p185/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون إن الآخرة خير وأبقى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r8.claim: The afterlife means Paradise, which is better than this world and lasts longer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r8.anchor: {والآخرة} أي والدار الآخرة يعني: الجنة. {خير} أفضل. {وأبقى} أدوم

WAHIDI-QT:87:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:17/r1.claim: The Hereafter is better than the worldly life and more enduring.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r1.claim: The afterlife is better than worldly life and more enduring.

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r5.claim: Because the afterlife is better and more enduring, intelligent people should choose it and work for purification and success; worldly preference inevitably ends in loss.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r5.anchor: âhiret daha hayırlı ve daha devamlıdır. Binâen‘aleyh fâni olan dünyâ hayat ne kadar zevkli olursa olsun âkil ve zeki olan insanların âhireti tercih ederek tezekkî ve felâha çalışmaları

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r6.claim: Those who choose the afterlife may endure worldly hardship without despair; their aim is to escape worldly pains and reach God's pleasure, not merely remain alive.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r6.anchor: dünyada ne kadar mihnet ve ıztırab görseler âkıbetten bedbin olmaz, ye’se düşmez, günden güne felah ve saadete doğru gitmeye ve hüsn-i hâtimeye muvaffak olurlar.

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r7.claim: The afterlife-oriented person gives the obligatory charity, remembers the Lord, and prays in preparation to meet him.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r7.anchor: başının vergisini verip Rabbinin ismini anarak O’na gitmek üzere namazını kılan, ibadetini yapan kimseler

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the vocabulary contrasting the present world and the hereafter, the note refers to Q 93:4.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu den für die Gegenüberstellung von Diesseits und Jenseits verwendeten Begrifflichkeiten vgl. die Anmerkung zu 93:4

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.claim: Second-person rebukes and the parallel growth of Quranic text and community make it unlikely that early proclamations presuppose a formed community or only follower-only devotional meetings.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.anchor: sprechen dagegen, als Sitz im Leben der frühen Verkündigungen lediglich auf Anhänger Muḥammads beschränkte Gemeindeandachten o. Ä. anzunehmen

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura shifts from God addressing the messenger to an abrupt, effective rebuke of hearers for worldly preference and rejection of the message’s core.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.anchor: Bis hier ist die Sure als Anrede Gottes an den Verkünder gehalten; sie wendet sich erst in einem

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.claim: The earlier typological contrast between good and bad now confronts hearers with a choice and its eschatological consequences.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.anchor: eingeführte Entgegensetzung von Guten und Bösen, von Seligen und Verdammten wird so in unmittelbaren Bezug zu den Hörern gesetzt

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.claim: People generally choose the temporary pleasures of worldly life over the hereafter, though the hereafter is better and everlasting; this warns unbelievers and counsels believers to avoid the same error (7:169; 12:109; 93:4).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.anchor: insanların genellikle geçici dünya hayatı ve zevklerini âhirete tercih ettikleri hatırlatılmaktadır

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r1.claim: “The Hereafter is better and more lasting” is a circumstantial clause reinforcing rebuke: its untainted pleasures are supremely delightful and everlasting.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r1.anchor: والآخرة خير وأبقى حال من فاعل تؤثرون مؤكدة للتوبيخ والعتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111/r2.claim: The verse does not spell out this world's troubles and short duration because their defects are obvious.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r3.claim: Ibn Masud explains that people prefer this life because its food, drink, women, pleasures, and beauty are immediate, while the hereafter is described but kept from them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r3.anchor: قال عرفجة الأشجعي: كنا عند ابن مسعود فقرأ هذه الآية، فقال لنا: أتدرون لم آثرنا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة؟ قلنا: لا قال: لأن الدنيا أحضرت

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r7.claim: The afterlife is better because its pleasure is intrinsic and free of harm, and it lasts without end.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r7.anchor: فإن نعيمها ملذ بالذات خالص عن الغوائل لا انقطاع له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r3.claim: The afterlife is the goal of creation and wiser than a purposeless world; its unclouded pleasure is better and permanently enduring, incomparable to what passes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r3.anchor: نعيم الآخرة دائم لا انقطاع له أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r4.claim: The rhetorical pairing leaves rejecting the afterlife implicit after mention of worldly preference, then uses the afterlife's goodness and permanence to imply the world's opposite; it deters from the base and attracts to the lasting.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.claim: The sura follows the warning against worldly preference with a warning against turning from purification through any route other than the prophets' method.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.anchor: رهب أول هذه من الإعراض عن ذلك مرة , ومن التزكي بغير منهاج الرسل

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.speaker: عرفجة الثقفي
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd stopped at the verse, confessed that they favored worldly life, and explained that its visible pleasures displaced the unseen afterlife; he also read the verb with yāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.anchor: عن عرفجة الثقفي قال: استقرأت ابن مسعود {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} فلما بلغ {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا}

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.claim: Qatāda says people choose immediate life except those God protects; the afterlife surpasses this life in goodness and permanence.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {خزي في الحياة الدنيا} قال: اختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله {والآخرة خير}

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet’s counsel that love for either world harms the other, so one should choose what lasts over what perishes.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet describing worldly life as the home and wealth of those lacking real home and wealth, gathered by the mindless.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.anchor: دار من لا دار له ومال من لا مال له

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.claim: Mūsā ibn Yasār reports that God created nothing more hated to Him than the world and has never looked at it.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.anchor: عن موسى بن يسار رضي الله عنه أنه بلغه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله جل ثناؤه لم يخلق خلقا أبغض إليه

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.claim: Qatāda says God’s scriptures agree in succession that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون إن الآخرة خير وأبقى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.claim: Qatāda also specifies that the earlier scrolls teach that the afterlife is better than worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} الآية قال: في الصحف الأولى إن الآخرة خير من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.claim: Asked whether the Prophet received anything from those scrolls, he recited the passage from purification and prayer through the superiority of the afterlife and the scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.anchor: هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال: يا أبا ذر نعم {قد أفلح من تزكى

ALUSI:87:17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:17/r1.claim: The clause about the Hereafter is circumstantial to the subject of you prefer, reinforcing rebuke and reproach.
ALUSI:87:17/r1.anchor: حال من فاعل { تؤثرون } مؤكد للتوبيخ والعتاب أي تؤثرونها على الآخرة

ALUSI:87:17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:17/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:17/r2.claim: The Hereafter is intrinsically better because its utmost delights are untainted and everlasting.
ALUSI:87:17/r2.anchor: أي تؤثرونها على الآخرة والحال أن الآخرة خير في نفسها لما أن نعيمها

ALUSI:87:17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:17/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:17/r3.claim: The text omits mention of the world's pleasure being spoiled by troubles and soon ending because that is self-evident.
ALUSI:87:17/r3.anchor: وعدم التعرض لبيان تكدر نعيم الدنيا بالمنغصات وانقطاعه عما قليل لغاية الظهور

BAGHAWI:87:17/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:17/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI:87:17/r1.claim: ʿArfaja al-Ashjaʿi reports that Ibn Masʿud explained preferring this life by its immediate food, drink, women, pleasures, and adornment, while the Hereafter is promised but unseen; people love the present and leave the deferred.
BAGHAWI:87:17/r1.anchor: قال عرفجة الأشجعي : كنا عند ابن مسعود فقرأ هذه الآية ، فقال لنا : أتدرون لم آثرنا الحياة الدنيا

BAYDAWI:87:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:17/r1.claim: The Hereafter is better because its pleasure is intrinsic and pure of harm, and it does not end.
BAYDAWI:87:17/r1.anchor: والآخرة خير وأبقى فإن نعيمها ملذ بالذات خالص عن الغوائل لا انقطاع له

BIQAI:87:17/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:17/r1.claim: The Hereafter is the exalted abode and the goal of creation and command; even conceding some good in this world, the next life is better because its bliss is wholly unspoiled.
BIQAI:87:17/r1.anchor: والحال أن الدار التي هي غاية الخلق ومقصود الأمر

BIQAI:87:17/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:17/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:17/r2.claim: The Hereafter endures without end; even a worldly life prolonged to its eventual passing would only count as lasting figuratively, so perishable bliss cannot compare.
BIQAI:87:17/r2.anchor: على تقدير المحال في الدنيا من أن تماديها إلى وقت زوالها تسمى بقاء ، لأن نعيم الآخرة دائم لا انقطاع له أصلاً

BIQAI:87:17/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:17/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:17/r3.claim: One who knows this clear truth pursues the Hereafter and rejects both sensory worldly attractions and imagined pleasures of the lower self.
BIQAI:87:17/r3.anchor: اشتغل بما يحصل الآخرة وينفي الدنيا بقسميها

BIQAI:87:17/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:17/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:17/r4.claim: The verse uses fitting ellipsis: preferring and lowliness first imply leaving and elevation second, while goodness and permanence second imply their opposites first; the order first deters, then attracts.
BIQAI:87:17/r4.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الإيثار والدنو أولاً

DURR:87:16/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:16/r4.claim: Qatada says people choose the present life except those God protects; the hereafter excels in goodness and lasts longer.
DURR:87:16/r4.anchor: عن قتادة { بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا } قال : اختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله

DURR:87:16/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:16/r7.claim: The Prophet says a person who meets God with the testimony enters Paradise unless it is mixed with love, preference, accumulation, and contentment with worldly life and the conduct of tyrants.
DURR:87:16/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «لا يلقى الله أحد بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

DURR:87:16/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:16/r8.claim: The Prophet says loving this world harms one’s hereafter, while loving the hereafter harms one’s worldly life, and urges choosing what endures over what perishes.
DURR:87:16/r8.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

DURR:87:17/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:17/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:17/r4.claim: Qatada says people choose the present life except those God protects; the hereafter excels in goodness and lasts longer.
DURR:87:17/r4.anchor: عن قتادة { بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا } قال : اختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله

DURR:87:17/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:17/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:17/r7.claim: The Prophet says a person who meets God with the testimony enters Paradise unless it is mixed with love, preference, accumulation, and contentment with worldly life and the conduct of tyrants.
DURR:87:17/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «لا يلقى الله أحد بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

DURR:87:17/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:17/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:17/r8.claim: The Prophet says loving this world harms one’s hereafter, while loving the hereafter harms one’s worldly life, and urges choosing what endures over what perishes.
DURR:87:17/r8.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

DURR:87:18/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:18/r5.claim: Qatada says God’s books succeed one another in teaching, as heard here: the hereafter is better and more enduring than the world.
DURR:87:18/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } قال : تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون

DURR:87:18/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:18/r6.claim: Qatada specifies the teaching in the earlier scrolls as the superiority of the hereafter over worldly life.
DURR:87:18/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } الآية ، قال : في الصحف الأولى إن الآخرة خير

IBNASHUR:87:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:17/r1.claim: The assertion that the hereafter is better and more lasting follows the rebuke, reinforcing it by showing what the audience has ignored.
IBNASHUR:87:17/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة التوبيخ عطف الخبر على الإنشاء

IBNASHUR:87:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:17/r2.claim: Abqā is a comparative meaning longer in duration.

IBNASHUR:87:17/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:17/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:87:17/r3.claim: A hadith about keeping a garment to the ankles calls that practice more God-fearing and more lasting.
IBNASHUR:87:17/r3.anchor: في حديث النهي عن جر الإزار « وليكن إلى الكعبين فإنه أتقى وأبقى »

IBNATIYYA:87:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:17/r1.claim: Preference for the immediate world comes from loving what is present and ignorance of the afterlife's permanence.
IBNATIYYA:87:17/r1.anchor: وسبب الإيثار حب العاجل والجهل ببقاء الآخرة

IBNATIYYA:87:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:17/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNATIYYA:87:17/r2.claim: ʿUmar compares everything in this world against the afterlife to a rabbit's puff of breath.
IBNATIYYA:87:17/r2.anchor: وقال عمر : ما في الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كنفخة أرنب

IBNKATHIR:87:17/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r1.claim: God’s reward in the afterlife is better and more lasting: this world is low and passing, while the next is noble and enduring, so a rational person should choose what lasts.
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r1.anchor: ثواب الله في الدار الآخرة خير من الدنيا وأبقى ، فإن الدنيا دنيَّة فانية ، والآخرة شريفة باقية

IBNKATHIR:87:17/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r2.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r2.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the world is a home for one without a home, wealth for one without wealth, and gathered for one without intellect; Ahmad transmits it.
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " الدنيا دار من لا دار له ، ومال من لا مال له ، ولها يجمع من لا عقل له "

IBNKATHIR:87:17/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r5.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r5.claim: The Prophet says that loving worldly life harms one’s afterlife and loving the afterlife harms one’s worldly life, so people should prefer what remains to what perishes; Ahmad alone transmits this report, also by another route.
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r5.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :  " من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

MAWARDI:87:17/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:17/r1.claim: The Hereafter is better for the believer than worldly life and more enduring in its recompense.
MAWARDI:87:17/r1.anchor: أحدهما : خير للمؤمن من الدنيا ، وأبقى للجزاء

MAWARDI:87:17/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:17/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:87:17/r2.claim: Qatāda takes the phrase to mean that the Hereafter is better in goodness and more enduring in permanence.
MAWARDI:87:17/r2.anchor: ما قاله قتادة خير في الخير وأبقى في البقاء

MAWARDI:87:17/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:17/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:17/r3.claim: A synthesis is that the Hereafter is better for the obedient and more enduring for the people of Paradise.
MAWARDI:87:17/r3.anchor: والآخرة خير لأهل الطاعة وأبقى على أهل الجنة

NASAFI:87:17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:17/r1.claim: The afterlife is better and more enduring.
NASAFI:87:17/r1.anchor: { والآخرة خَيْرٌ وأبقى } أفضل من نفسها وأدوم

QURTUBI:87:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:17/r1.claim: Al-ākhira refers here to the abode of the afterlife, namely Paradise.

QURTUBI:87:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:17/r2.claim: The afterlife is better, meaning superior, and more lasting than the present world.
QURTUBI:87:17/r2.anchor: " خير " أي أفضل . " وأبقى " أي أدوم من الدنيا

QURTUBI:87:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:17/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:17/r3.claim: The Prophet compares the world in relation to the afterlife to a finger dipped in the sea, and asks what it brings back; al-Qurṭubī labels the report sound.
QURTUBI:87:17/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كما يضع أحدكم أصبعه في اليم

QURTUBI:87:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:17/r4.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI:87:17/r4.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār argues that even if the world were perishing gold and the afterlife enduring pottery, one should choose the latter; in fact the afterlife is enduring gold and this world perishing pottery.
QURTUBI:87:17/r4.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار : لو كانت الدنيا من ذهب يفنى

RAZI:87:17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:17/r1.claim: Whatever is better and more enduring deserves preference; the afterlife is therefore more deserving than the worldly life that people choose.
RAZI:87:17/r1.anchor: أن كل ما كان خيرا وأبقى فهو آثر ، فيلزم أن تكون الآخرة آثر من الدنيا

RAZI:87:17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:17/r2.claim: The afterlife is better because it contains both bodily and spiritual happiness, unlike worldly life.

RAZI:87:17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:17/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:17/r3.claim: Worldly pleasures are mixed with pain, whereas the afterlife’s pleasures are not.
RAZI:87:17/r3.anchor: أن الدنيا لذاتها مخلوطة بالآلام ، والآخرة ليست كذلك

RAZI:87:17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:17/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:17/r4.claim: The afterlife lasts while the world perishes, and what endures is better than what perishes.
RAZI:87:17/r4.anchor: أن الدنيا فانية ، والآخرة باقية ، والباقي خير من الفاني

ITQAN:v3p268/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p268/r2.claim: A comparative can omit what it is being compared with: 'knows the secret and what is more hidden' and 'better and more enduring.'
ITQAN:v3p268/r2.anchor: ومنه حذف متعلق أفعل التفضيل نحو ﴿ يعلم السر وأخفى ﴾ ﴿ خير وأبقى ﴾

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r24.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r24.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r24.claim: For believers who seek it, the afterlife is better and more enduring than this world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.claim: Disbelievers prefer transient life to the better, eternal afterlife, so the Prophet's message finds no root in their hearts despite its continuity with earlier prophetic teaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.anchor: giving preference to this world over the next

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.claim: The Quraysh's hostility comes from attachment to worldly interests: they invent doubts rather than risk those interests for the Hereafter, sacrificing eternal reward for transient life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.anchor: the Hereafter is more lasting and permanent
